title: Company Orbit — Planning Bridge Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
- Create a compact, operational playbook to bridge current-quarter execution into the company OKR draft and the next all-hands.
- Provide the exec team a short run-of-show and signal map so we align messages, asks, and risks before the town meeting.

Context / background (short):
- Growth in Dedicated customers and Private inbound RFIs increased Q1 operating noise. Engineering is shipping multiple infra fixes while Product finalizes rollout gating for Redwood Optimize.
- Leadership wants a single, tight narrative that: a) acknowledges reliability pressure, b) shows measurable progress on cost/perf levers, and c) gives GTM clear asks for customer-facing comms and enterprise pilots.

Target audiences:
- All-hands: entire company (engineers, product, go-to-market, support)
- Exec update: CEO, CTO, CFO, Heads of Eng/Product/GTM
- OKR reviewers: board, exec, key managers

High-level objectives for this playbook:
1) Align executive narrative and three company-level OKR candidates (v0.3).
2) Produce a 12-minute all-hands segment + Q&A script and backup slides.
3) Surface 5 cross-functional asks with owners and deadlines that GTM + Solutions can action post-all-hands.

Draft company OKRs (v0.3) — executive candidates (short form):
O1: Make inference predictable at scale for production customers.
- KR1: Reduce 95th pctile inference latency by 20% for top-10% of routes (by traffic) by end of quarter.
- KR2: Decrease per-token serving cost for hosted API by 15% through batching and quantization recommendations.
- KR3: Launch two Dedicated capacity customers on SLA-backed configs with <2% service interruptions.

O2: Expand enterprise adoption for private deployments while preserving security posture.
- KR1: Close 4 Private deals (signed contracts) with audit/KMS support integrated.
- KR2: Publish Private deployment reference architecture + partner integration kit.
- KR3: Achieve SOC-type checklist completion for two top target accounts.

O3: Improve developer velocity and observability to reduce regression risk.
- KR1: Ship Redwood Console per-route tracing in GA to internal customers and onboard 3 pilot apps.
- KR2: Reduce mean time to detect (MTTD) for inference regressions by 30% via alerting/playbooks.
- KR3: Run continuous evals against canonical prompt set weekly and close top-5 regressions.

Notes on KRs: these are intentionally product/operational KRs that can be measured via Console dashboards. We should surface baseline numbers in the next revision (v0.4) and add numeric owners.

All-hands segment (12-minute plan) — run of show (draft):
- 0:00–0:30 (Host): quick house-keeping + one-line company status.
- 0:30–6:00 (CEO): Narrative: market opportunity, what winning looks like (30–60s per signal). Script bullets attached below.
- 6:00–9:00 (CTO): What we've shipped / reliability story / three product examples tied to OKRs. Call out Dedicated wins and Private sprint.
- 9:00–11:00 (Head of Console/Product): Observable metrics + short demo of per-route tracing (recorded).
- 11:00–12:00 (Customer success): One short customer quote and ask for internal pairing.
- Q&A (15 minutes): pre-seeded two Qs from leadership + open mic.

Speaker bullets (prep):
- CEO: one-sentence market thesis (why serving matters now), three signals we delivered (product, customers, reliability), two asks (shorten PR turnaround for top-customer blockers; enable sales with pilot playbook).
- CTO: explicit metrics (latency delta, cost improvement, incidents reduced), what’s next (canary rollout plan), contingency (fallback model routing).

Top five cross-functional asks (post-all-hands):
1) GTM: publish pilot playbook + two sales one-pagers for Private in 3 weeks — owner: Priya (GTM).
2) Eng infra: complete KV cache rollout on staging clusters — owner: Diego — deadline: 2025-03-05.
3) Console: expose KR dashboards and add alerting for top-10 routes — owner: Maya — deadline: 2025-03-12.
4) Solutions: prepare 2 reference architectures for regulated sectors — owner: Arman — deadline: 2025-03-19.
5) Customer success: assemble the top-20 enterprise health signals and sharing cadence — owner: Asha — deadline: 2025-03-08.

Risks and mitigations (short list):
- Risk: Messaging mismatch will create customer confusion if we surface incomplete Private timelines.
  Mitigation: Have a single sentence ‘what to expect’ and a public-private timeline (estimated) and escalate any inbound RFIs to Solutions.
- Risk: Engineering capacity concentrated on hotfixes undermines feature cadence.
  Mitigation: Temporary allocation: two-week triage to close sev1 fixes, then rotation back to OKR work, track in weekly heatmap.
- Risk: Console demo fails during live demo.
  Mitigation: Use recorded demo and have a runbook + fallback slide.

Decision points for execs ahead of finalizing OKRs (needed by 2025-02-24):
- Narrow to three KRs for O1 (pick most measurable; baseline numbers required).
- Confirm enterprise ask list for GTM (which verticals to prioritize: FinServ vs Healthcare).
- Approve the all-hands 12-minute cadence and the two pre-seeded Qs.

Open questions / things to resolve:
- Do we want cost reduction KRs expressed as absolute $/1M tokens or % relative to current quarters?
- Which two Dedicated customers can we surface as public case studies for the all-hands?
- Is the SOC-type checklist scope adequate for legal sign-off for Private deals? (Legal to confirm).

Communications plan (short):
- Pre-all-hands (one week out): internal teaser email with top-line OKR candidates + 1–page explainer for managers to prep their squads. (Owner: People Ops + Comms).
- Day of: 1-pager with asks and link to follow-up action items (Confluence) + curated Slack thread for Q&A.
- Post: publish recording, action tracker with owners & deadlines, and a heatmap check-in in two weeks.

Appendix — quick manager prep guide (for the 1-pager):
- One-sentence summary to read in team standups.
- Top-3 ways the team contributes to the OKRs this quarter.
- Any stop-the-line risks to escalate (two-line form).

TODOs (short):
- [Jordan] Draft v0.4 OKRs with baselines (due 2025-02-21).
- [Asha] Confirm customer quote and legal permission for callout (due 2025-02-20).
- [Maya] Golden recording of Console demo + slides (due 2025-02-23).
- [Riley] Finalize run-of-show and Q&A seeding (due 2025-02-24).

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intentionally terse. Please add comments inline or reply in Slack thread #company-orbit on suggestions. We will iterate to v0.4 with numerical baselines and explicit KR owners.

Historic context: pulled lessons from last two all-hands where demo flaked and messaging created downstream support churn; those incidents are summarized in confluence:company/allhands-postmortem-2024.

End of doc.
